title: Apple TV Unveils Justin Timberlake Documentary Trailer and Four-Part Release Schedule
excerpt:
Fisher Stevens directs a four-part series examining Justin Timberlake's career.
The Apple TV documentary begins December 11, 2026.
body_md:
Apple TV has confirmed the release schedule for Timberlake, a four-part documentary directed by Academy Award winner Fisher Stevens. The first two episodes arrive on Friday, December 11, 2026, followed by episode three on December 18 and the finale on December 23. The announcement follows an earlier report about the project.

The series spans roughly three decades of Timberlake's career and public life. It revisits his childhood, his rise with NSYNC and his transition to solo stardom, while also addressing personal challenges and the pressures associated with a long career in the public eye. Producers say the documentary features previously unseen archival footage and exclusive interviews with relatives, friends and collaborators.

The newly released trailer signals that two especially scrutinized chapters will receive attention: Timberlake's former relationship with Britney Spears and the controversy surrounding his performance with Janet Jackson during the 2004 Super Bowl halftime show. The preview moves between youthful footage, memories of early celebrity and images of those two artists.

Timberlake's narration contrasts lighthearted childhood memories with experiences that are difficult to discuss. One sequence shows a teenage Timberlake displaying a Janet Jackson poster in his bedroom, before the preview shifts to footage involving Spears. Jessica Biel, Timberlake's wife, also appears in the trailer, alongside other people associated with his life.

The preview establishes the subjects the filmmakers intend to examine, but it does not yet establish the depth of each discussion or whether every person shown participates in a new interview. In particular, the balance between Timberlake's own account and the perspectives of others involved in past controversies remains something audiences will have to assess after release.

Blackbird Presents Films, Misher Films and Highly Flammable produced the documentary for Apple TV, with Maura Anderson and Stevens serving as producers. Executive producers include Kevin Misher, Keith Wortman and several other industry figures. The series is presented by Live Nation Studios.

Beyond its celebrity profile, the project raises a broader question about how a major pop star narrates decades of acclaim and public criticism in retrospect. The confirmed facts are the release dates, creative team and subjects previewed in the trailer; the documentary's eventual conclusions should not be assumed in advance.
